strategy.summary: Reproduce the INT_MIN abs-overflow in npy_gcd by building NumPy from source at the buggy commit 9f24013e3e78 and running the project's test_gcd_overflow in test_umath.py. The defect is undefined behaviour from negating INT_MIN, so it is only confirmed to manifest on s390x with GCC 11.5. The transition is therefore only established on that platform; elsewhere the buggy build may pass.

pinned_because: numpy is not documented and no version is pinned by the evidence; the reproduction must come from source at the buggy commit rather than a released wheel, because the bug lives in the C source of npy_gcd
pytest and hypothesis are documented in README.md with no constraint, so the latest compatible versions are chosen and this is not numerically relevant
Python version is null in the evidence; use the Python version the checked-out revision's build requirements support
GCC 11.5 is reported in trigger_conditions, but the evidence does not pin it as a build requirement, so it is a platform condition rather than a pin

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 9f24013e3e78 built on s390x with GCC 11.5, test_gcd_overflow fails: for an INT_MIN input the assert_equal compares np.gcd against q and sees a negative value (-536870912 for int32) instead of 536870912, so the test FAILS. On the fixed revision, where abs is computed via unsigned negation, all four dtype iterations (int8, int16, int32, int64) pass for both INT_MIN argument orders, so the test PASSES.
strategy.numerical_probe: Compile a small C harness of the original npy_gcd abs expression with -fsanitize=undefined and feed it INT_MIN to confirm the UB is reached on any platform, which shows the defect exists even where the test does not flip.
risks: The transition is only observed on s390x with GCC 11.5. On x86_64 or aarch64 the wrapped negation may produce the correct value, so the buggy build may pass and the test will not transition. Do not treat a pass on other platforms as a failed reproduction.
No s390x runner is assumed. If the environment is not s390x, the test cannot be expected to fail on the buggy revision, and the strategy cannot be confirmed there.
Optimisation level and compiler flags can change whether the UB manifests; the build must use the default flags of the checked-out revision with GCC 11.5 to match the report.
The int8 and int16 iterations were added in the fixed test and were not in the original test, so their buggy behaviour is not part of the originally reported evidence and may differ.

The evidence's test_commands include numpy.test() and a one-line python -c reproducer. numpy.test is not the project test and the one-liner is not the developer's test, so neither is used as the success gate.
numpy version is unbounded and undocumented in the evidence; the issue reports 2.4.4 in the reporter's environment, but building from the buggy commit overrides that choice.
Test class name TestRationalFunctions is taken from the oracle clue, not from the diff hunk, so it should be verified against the file before relying on the node id.

oracle.reference_source: the test's own assert_equal against q, computed as -(a // 4)
oracle.why: gcd of integers is exact, so the expected value 536870912 is compared with no tolerance

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the s390x GCC 11.5 buggy build, assert_equal receives -536870912 where it expects 536870912, so AssertionError is raised; the negation of INT_MIN in a < 0 ? -a : a is undefined and wraps to INT_MIN, which yields a negative gcd. On x86 this may not occur, so the assertion may not fire there.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The fixed build takes abs through an unsigned cast before negation, so gcd returns 536870912 for every dtype and argument order on the affected platform; the PR author reports PASS after the fix.
